newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy set to miss Maastricht goal - banking group.
newsitem.headline: Italy set to miss Maastricht goal - banking group.

text.p: Italy will not reduce its deficit to gross domestic product (GDP) ratio to three percent next year unless there is an unexpected surge in the economy, the Italian Banking Association (ABI) said.

In its yearly outlook, ABI forecast that Italy's deficit/GDP ratio would be four percent next year against the government's 3.1 percent target and the 3.0 percent level established by the Maastricht treaty for countries wishing to sign up to the planned single European currency.
ABI said that Italy's adehsion to the Maastricht treaty would have to wait "at least" until 1998.
The banking association was also pessimistic about the government's chances of meeting its goal of average annual inflation of 2.5 percent next year.
It saw inflation at three percent during 1997. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
